reviews.text: The doctor's dedication to saving lives is wonderful! His firm stance on what's wrong shows his strength as a doctor and makes him trustworthy. The staff are also supportive, offering advice and encouragement. This is a hospital where both animals and their owners can feel at ease.

This is a great hospital with a kind director who clearly loves animals, and compassionate staff. I'm truly grateful for the efforts you made with treatment and lifestyle guidance to make the time my pet had left after becoming bedridden as long and enjoyable as possible.

I used their services several years ago.

It was a veterinary clinic recommended by a relative when I got my first pet (a cat).

I took my cat there for neutering surgery and for its early growth.

I remember them providing emergency care at night when one of my cats dislocated a toe on its front leg.

It was far from where I lived at the time, so I switched to a closer veterinary clinic, but everyone there was so kind, which eased my anxieties about owning a pet for the first time.

I'm writing this review because I finished raising my cats this summer.

Thank you so much.

This clinic does not accept reservations; patients are seen on a first-come, first-served basis. The doctor is efficient, and the nurses, though few in number, work diligently, resulting in a quick turnover. Despite being busy, everyone is kind. It's a warm and welcoming hospital.

It's popular and tends to get crowded, but there are only four waiting chairs, and dogs, cats (and rabbits, etc.) all share the same waiting room. Even when busy, you rarely have to wait a long time.

* They do not have an X-ray machine.
* Examinations are performed using ultrasound.

My cat received treatment here.

A tumor suddenly appeared on her abdomen, and after removal and examination, it was found to be cancerous.

Other tumors were found inside the body and removed. We continued taking the cat for medication and follow-up appointments, but we were told that "there were actually other sites of metastasis," and a few days later, my cat passed away.

Ultrasound has its limitations; if it had been confirmed with an X-ray, the tumor could have been removed earlier, and my cat might still be alive and healthy (though this is only a possibility).

●For patients with symptoms requiring an X-ray,
(1) Have an X-ray taken elsewhere and bring it with you (you can sometimes get a paper copy).
(2) Take your cat to another animal hospital that has an X-ray machine.
...I recommend these options.

・For vaccinations and health checkups, I recommend this hospital; it's warm, efficient, and has a pleasant atmosphere.

I first visited this clinic three years ago, shortly after my beloved toy poodle was diagnosed with diabetes. I went to a hospital thinking it might be kidney disease, but they diagnosed it as diabetes, and I was referred here.

It's a family-run clinic, and on my first visit, the wife, a nurse, gave my dog ​​a huge piece of cheese—more than a centimeter cube!

All I could say was, "Huh?"

Even when my dog ​​was healthy, I'd never given him cheese... Is it really okay to give such a large piece of cheese to a diabetic toy poodle???

I was shocked.

Furthermore, the female veterinarian is the head doctor's daughter, and despite her limited experience, she gives rather careless advice...
When my dog's blood sugar spiked and the head doctor told me, "Don't do things without consulting me!", I mentioned that I'd consulted the daughter, but she gave me a vague, evasive answer.

As a result, when we went to the mentor of this hospital director, our dog was diagnosed with two complications and was admitted immediately.

★Due to the lack of proper care at Takama Animal Hospital, our dog's eyes quickly deteriorated due to persistent high blood sugar. When he had an epileptic seizure due to hypoglycemia, we were told to "get used to it."

This is terrible treatment, considering that prolonged epileptic seizures can be fatal.

While our dog was staying there for a long time for diabetes testing,
someone left a miniature dachshund with heart problems there.

The dog wasn't even put in an oxygen chamber, developed cyanosis, and died.

Before my current dog, I had a toy poodle that I rescued and cared for, and it had terminal heart disease. At home, I always carried nitroglycerin with me on walks.

On its last day, I used nitroglycerin, but it didn't work, so we tried mouth-to-mouth resuscitation to try and revive it.

Even after all that, it didn't work, so I gave up and let her cross the rainbow bridge. But even if you leave your pet at this hospital, they won't treat it properly; they'll just survive.

I wouldn't recommend this hospital for pets with life-threatening illnesses.

I visited after a neighbor recommended the place. Since it was my first time visiting a veterinary clinic in Japan, I was a bit anxious, but the director and the nurses... were so attentive and caring that I was deeply moved.

They showed such consideration by explaining things in simple Japanese to me, a foreigner. They used materials and photos to make it easy for me to understand, despite my lack of knowledge regarding veterinary medicine, and highlighted the key points regarding the treatment goals and follow-up care. In particular... they didn't just tell me the results; they even explained why this treatment was necessary and what impact it would have on my dog... They are so thoughtful 🥹🥹

I already knew that Japan has an advanced animal culture, but I was truly touched not only by their technology but also by their affection for animals and the warmth with which they treated an anxious owner.

I am so happy and grateful to have found a trustworthy veterinary clinic... ! 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻
